A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReportLogic benchmark and LogicJudge study. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original judge-agreement results, a three-domain model leaderboard, human annotation experiments, rubric ablations, and adversarial evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports per-dimension human agreement and qualitative rubric-generator comparisons.

M1.justification: The taxonomy, context-aware rubric pipeline, ensemble distillation, and SFT/GRPO training remain unchanged. Figure 12 replaces an illustrative Tie label with both good/both bad, aligning the example with requirements already present in v1 Appendix A.1 and Figure 12's constraints.

E1.justification: Both versions use DeepResearch, Zhihu, and Quora with the same report-generation and logical-evaluation tasks. The added attack excerpts illustrate existing attack types; corrected query counts do not establish expanded dataset or scenario coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix C.2 newly reports a qualitative rubric-generator comparison involving Gemini-2.5-Pro, GPT-5.1, and the selected Claude-4.5-Sonnet. The main judge comparison retains the same 16 LLMs and two ensembles; changing the stated count from 17 to 16 corrects the description.

E3.justification: Appendix C.4 changes targeted-attack success from preferring the attacked report to preferring it or tying on the targeted dimension. Section 5.1 also changes query counts from 1,319/847/915 to 1,204/1,262/1,198, matching the already-existing appendix table. These are reported protocol corrections; the PDFs do not establish reruns or changed data collection.

E4.justification: v2 extends the rubric analysis with per-dimension human agreement and qualitative generator-selection findings. New Table 5 provides five original/attacked report pairs illustrating three targeted defects and two surface manipulations. The existing rubric ablation, bad-case analysis, and attack suites remain.

E5.justification: The new dimension-level agreement rows use the existing Fleiss' kappa reporting practice. Neither version introduces different repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance testing, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports eight General-Rubric/Context-Aware kappa pairs, including Internal Consistency at 0.35/0.42 and Warrants at 0.73/0.73. Appendix C.2 adds qualitative generator rankings and reports no rubric JSON-schema violations. Table 1 and the existing performance plots retain their results; no plotted update accompanies the revised targeted-ASR definition.

T1.justification: Appendix C.4 revises the defined success event underlying targeted ASR: its numerator now includes ties on the attacked dimension. This is a limited metric-definition change. The SFT loss, GRPO objective, reward equations, and existing kappa formula remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about ReportLogic, specialized LogicJudge evaluation, and judge vulnerabilities. The additional evidence does not redefine or strengthen those central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds a rationale connecting auditability to decision-support use, attributes rubric schema compliance to constrained prompting and instruction following, and explains why ties count differently for targeted and surface-bias attacks. The limitations section and established explanations of judge failure modes remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a concrete code/data repository link, rubric-generator selection and verification details, and explicit attack-screening criteria covering isolation, minimal edits, and bounded strength. It also corrects the training-prompt example. These expand documentation of existing procedures; hardware, training budgets, and hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 substantially expands positioning through dedicated discussions of rubric-guided evaluation and trained LLM judges. It distinguishes instance-specific rubrics from fixed schemes and LogicJudge from general-purpose evaluators, adding references to Prometheus, Generative Reward Models, Skywork-Reward-v2, and the MT-Bench/Chatbot Arena judging study.

P1.justification: v2 expands related-work and appendix explanations, adds local subheadings, and corrects grammar and cross-references. The overall section sequence, central narrative, and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the per-dimension agreement table and paired attack-example table, with accompanying layout shifts. It corrects spelling in Figure 2, changes Figure 3's color-bar label from LogicBench to ReportLogic, and reformats Figure 12. Existing figures and tables are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through dimension-level annotation evidence, concrete attack examples, clearer quality-control documentation, an explicit code/data link, and corrected reporting. The gains are limited by an unresolved inconsistency: Appendix C.4 includes ties in targeted ASR, while Figure 5 retains its preference-only caption and unchanged plot. Overall, the additions modestly improve the paper without establishing stronger main performance results.
